question: Your support agent, built with the Claude Agent SDK, calls the process_refund MCP tool after it approves a return. When the payment gateway is unavailable, process_refund returns the message "Refund not submitted: gateway unavailable" as a normal successful result. The agent then confirms to customers that their refund is complete. How should process_refund communicate this failure back to the agent?

options.text: Return a successful result with a refund status of pending, so the agent tells the customer that the refund will arrive later.
options.reason: This still reports the failure as a success and gives the customer false information, instead of using the isError flag to signal the failure.

options.text: Return the failure text in a longer and more detailed successful result, so the agent has more context to notice that the refund failed.
options.reason: The result is still marked as successful, so the agent must guess from the text; the isError flag is the pattern that tells the agent the call failed.

options.text: Return the gateway failure details in the tool result with the isError flag set to true, so the agent knows the refund failed.
options.reason: The MCP isError flag pattern is how a tool tells the agent that a call failed, so the agent stops treating the failure as a completed refund.

options.text: Record the gateway failure only in a server log and return the normal confirmation text, so the customer conversation continues without disruption.
options.reason: The agent never learns about the failure, so it cannot make a recovery decision; the guide says failures must be communicated back to the agent with the isError flag.
